Validate and organise case-control step data

Source: R/data.R
prepare_ssf_data.Rd

Each ID must identify an independent, uninterrupted segment. Supply separate IDs across observation gaps, even for the same animal. Strata follow their first appearance in the input; rows are reordered within strata to put the case first. If time is supplied, case times must increase within each segment. No incomplete stratum or nonfinite value is silently removed. If you rearrange rows after preparation, prepare the original data again before fitting. Prepared choice sets must remain contiguous and case-first.

Usage

prepare_ssf_data(
  data,
  id = "ID",
  stratum = "stratum",
  observed = "obs",
  weight = "w",
  time = NULL,
  density_measure = c("unspecified", "area", "step_angle"),
  expected_interval = NULL,
  step_max = Inf
)

Arguments

data

A data frame of observed and control steps.

id, stratum, observed, weight

Names of the segment, choice set, binary observation, and positive sampling density columns. Weights may be proportional to the conditioned proposal within a choice set when interpreting conditional choice probabilities. Absolute emission densities require the correctly normalised proposal on the availability domain.

time

Optional name of a numeric or POSIXct observation time column.

density_measure

Measure of the supplied sampling density: "area", "step_angle", or "unspecified". This annotation records the convention; it does not alter or verify weights.

expected_interval

Optional positive interval between consecutive cases within a segment. Requires time. Units are seconds for POSIXct, otherwise the units of the numeric time column. Gaps cause an error.

step_max

Upper radial support in step-length units, or Inf for unbounded support. Declare the radius of a common availability disk here. Finite support currently uses the canonical importance kernel.

Value

A validated data frame of class ssf_data, with standard columns ID, stratum, obs, and w, and a .source_row mapping.

Examples

d <- data.frame(ID = 1, stratum = rep(1:3, each = 2),
                obs = rep(c(1, 0), 3), w = 1, step = 1:6)
prepare_ssf_data(d)
#>   ID stratum obs w step .source_row  log_step
#> 1  1       1   1 1    1           1 0.0000000
#> 2  1       1   0 1    2           2 0.6931472
#> 3  1       2   1 1    3           3 1.0986123
#> 4  1       2   0 1    4           4 1.3862944
#> 5  1       3   1 1    5           5 1.6094379
#> 6  1       3   0 1    6           6 1.7917595
